prompt:
You are sitting in the cockpit looking out at the depths of space, with panels of electronics around you, whirring bleeps and lights, and the sleek, subtle glow of gently used screens. The style combines the analog buzz and grit of 80s science fiction like Alien and Star Wars with the sleek, translucent white glow of modern science fiction tech, plus a bit of digital crush in homage to the original Asteroids.

Create a bold, inviting whole-screen HANGAR concept for the game Astronomical, 16:9. It should scratch the gritty sci-fi fantasy itch. Make a compelling piece of ship equipment with a distinctive screen, grounded in the supplied images.

Image roles, in the exact supplied order:
Image 1, chosen-ink-finish.png: OWNER-SELECTED FINISH. Carry its hand-drawn ink contours, broad hard light/shadow planes and tactile drawn edges into the new hardware. Its old composition and old generic screen rows are not the design to copy.
Image 2, real-hangar-capture.png: REAL GAME SCENE AND SHIP. Use this nebula/starfield and this exact Vanguard design and livery. Give the ship a generous, central viewing area with clear breathing room. It may be repositioned for the new composition.
Image 3, 03-beige-console-schematic.png: HARDWARE MOOD. Borrow recessed screen depth, installed equipment, purposeful secondary mechanisms and warm room light.
Image 4, 09-beige-console-wireframe.png: HARDWARE AND SCREEN ORGANIZATION MOOD. Borrow the screen within chunky equipment, function-key-style tabs and a narrow side data column.
Image 5, 04-dark-cockpit-leds.png: SURROUNDING ELECTRONICS MOOD. Borrow grouped service modules, small banks of warm amber and dim green lights, and rich dark masses around bright instruments. Render that richness in the chosen ink-and-shade finish.
Image 6, 01-nostromo-terminal.webp: SCREEN LANGUAGE. Borrow its raster lettering, inverse-video blocks, thick screen divisions, layout rhythm and luminous strokes.
Image 7, 06-muthur-terminal-text.png: SCREEN LETTERING AND TEXTURE. Borrow its readable terminal type and gentle phosphor/raster irregularity.
Image 8, 07-hatched-progress-bars.webp: SCREEN MARKS. Borrow its confident lines, hatching and contrast. Use hatching as separator texture; only display actual information supplied below.
The mood references contribute feeling and visual language. Use the game scene and the content below for subject matter.

Screen content is the current hangar loadout only: HANGAR; SHIP / Vanguard; ENGINE / Default_Engine; SHIELD / Default_Shield; PRIMARY / Lasers; SECONDARY / Missiles; LAUNCH. Show the same choices and selection chevrons with a new terminal composition. Make HANGAR an inverse-video title bar. Use a side column for those real loadout names and function-key-like tabs labelled with the existing categories, without inventing keyboard shortcuts. Warm off-white screen ink, readable terminal/raster lettering, tick rules, clear large/small text hierarchy and purposeful inverse selection marks. Make the screen itself full of reference character instead of five modern web-form boxes. Actual font selection remains provisional.

Hardware has purposeful electronics, a few service latches, heat fins, cable guards and lights placed to explain how it is assembled. Strong ink silhouettes and sculpted shadow planes make the detail readable. Charcoal structure and dark recessed screens carry the mass, with warm-grey lit faces as accents. Amber and dim green hardware lamps. Use reusable straight edges and roughly 40-degree chamfered corners. Hardware stays attached to the foreground ship structure while the open scene remains the largest area. Compose both screen and ship as important parts of the whole picture. Keep the ship completely visible.

Keep real loadout content only, without invented telemetry or extra numbers. Preserve the Vanguard identity. Output just the polished whole-screen concept, without presentation captions, watermarks or logos.

COMPOSITION B: OFFSET INSTRUMENT POD.
Design a compact upright ship-computer pod emerging from the lower-left on a short dark mechanical support, with a bright recessed terminal face and purposeful electronics attached to one shoulder. The face has an inverse title strip, strong divisions and the narrow loadout side column. Beside it, separated by a visible gap, a lower control module holds LAUNCH and a restrained bank of physical lamps. Dark mounting structure makes both clearly part of the cockpit instead of floating windows. Emphasize an expressive irregular equipment silhouette, readable individual systems and layered ink shadows. Give the hero Vanguard a large clear viewing area around the center/right, balanced against the pod rather than trapped in a corner. Space remains visible between and around the grounded hardware. Avoid a continuous light wall along the whole left and bottom.
